transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I used to be able to focus for hours on designs, but now my mind feels foggy and I can’t make even basic decisions at work. My manager eventually noticed how much I was struggling with the stress and suggested the employee assistance program, which is what led to this referral.

Can you tell me more about how this foggy feeling and difficulty making decisions started, was it sudden or did it come on gradually, and have you experienced any significant stressful events recently?

It came on gradually after I transitioned to a full-time engineering technician role on a high-pressure aerospace project about fourteen months ago, which had tight deadlines and a demanding supervisor. I tried to cope by working longer hours, but the constant stress eventually wore me down until my brain felt full of static. Now, making even basic decisions at work or just deciding what to eat for dinner completely paralyzes me.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, such as designing, since you started feeling this way?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love. Activities like tinkering with 3-D printers, running with my track club, or playing board games just feel flat and pointless now. Instead of doing any of that, I usually just end up sitting on my couch scrolling through old work emails.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty or worthless about your inability to perform at work or enjoy the activities you used to love?

Yes, I constantly feel like a complete fraud who shouldn't have been hired, and I lie awake replaying tiny work mistakes, feeling like I don't even deserve my degree. Not being able to enjoy running or 3-D printing anymore makes me feel even more useless, like I'm just wasting away on the couch.
Can you describe a specific situation recently where you felt overwhelmed by these feelings of guilt or worthlessness, and how you responded to them?

The other night, I lay awake for hours replaying a tiny dimension error I made in a CAD file, feeling like a complete fraud who doesn't even deserve my degree. I was convinced I was dragging the entire team down with my incompetence, so I just lay there paralyzed in the dark, overwhelmed by the feeling that everyone would be better off without me.
Have you experienced any traumatic events, either recently or in the past, that might be contributing to your feelings of guilt, worthlessness, or being overwhelmed?

No, I can't think of any specific traumatic events in my past or recently. I think my feelings of guilt and being overwhelmed really stem from the intense pressure, the demanding supervisor, and the heavy workload of transitioning into this full-time aerospace engineering role.

You mentioned that these feelings started about fourteen months ago, but can you tell me if there was a period where your symptoms significantly worsened or if they have been steadily increasing over this time?

They have been steadily increasing and getting worse over time rather than spiking suddenly. At first, I tried to cope by working harder, but over the months my boundaries eroded, I stopped my hobbies, and the cognitive fog set in. It was only after I had already slid into this heavy, joyless state that the paranoid thoughts and the voice in my head eventually started.

You mentioned that your symptoms have been steadily increasing over the past fourteen months, but can you tell me if there was a distinct period, even if brief, where you felt relatively better or if the worsening has been continuous without any significant improvements?

It has been pretty constant, and this heavy depression, guilt, and foggy thinking have hung over me most days for a little over a year. However, on the very rare days when my mood and energy feel a bit closer to normal, those paranoid feelings and the voice in my head pretty much disappear. It is only during those brief moments that I get any kind of break from it.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been steadily worsening over the past fourteen months, but can you clarify if there was ever a two-week period or more during this time where you felt significantly better, or has the depression been persistent without any notable periods of improvement?

No, there has never been a two-week period where I felt significantly better or back to normal. The heavy fog and guilt have been persistent almost every single day for over a year now. I only get very rare, isolated days where my mood feels slightly closer to normal, but otherwise it has been continuous.

You mentioned that your symptoms have been persistent for over a year, but can you confirm if you've had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt completely back to your normal self, without any depressive symptoms, for at least two weeks?

No, I can definitely confirm I haven't had any two-week periods where I felt completely back to normal. This heavy depression has been constant for over a year now, with no real break from the symptoms. Even on the rare single day where I feel slightly closer to my usual self, it never lasts and I don't feel fully recovered.
Have you experienced any periods of elevated mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep that lasted for several days or more at any point in the past fourteen months?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that—no periods of high energy, elevated mood, or needing less sleep. On the rare days when I feel a bit better, my energy and mood just feel closer to my normal baseline. I certainly don't feel hyper, high, or overly energetic.
Can you confirm if you have experienced two or more major depressive episodes in the past, with at least two months of recovery in between, or has this been a single continuous episode?

This has been a single, continuous episode. It started a little over a year ago, a few months after I transitioned into the full-time aerospace position, and it has been ongoing every day since. I haven't had any periods of recovery or felt like my old self at all during this time.

You've described a single, continuous episode of depressive symptoms over the past year, but can you think of any periods, even if brief, where you felt a significant reduction in symptoms for at least a couple of months before they returned, or has it been a steady, unbroken period of depression?

No, it has been a steady, unbroken period of depression with absolutely no extended relief since it started. I have never had a break of a couple of months where I felt better. At most, I only experience rare, isolated days where I feel slightly closer to normal, but the heavy, foggy feeling always returns immediately.

Can you confirm whether you have had any previous episodes of depression before this current one that has lasted over a year, or is this your first experience with such persistent depressive symptoms?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is the first time in my life that I've ever felt this level of persistent depression and heavy fog.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt completely free of depressive symptoms, or has this been the only episode in your life?

This is the only episode I've ever experienced in my life. Since it started a little over a year ago, I haven't had any break from the symptoms at all, let alone a two-month period of feeling normal. It has just been one continuous, heavy fog.

Given that you've experienced a single, continuous episode of depression for over a year without any significant periods of recovery, can you confirm if you've ever had any periods of normal mood or significant symptom reduction that lasted for at least two weeks, which might help differentiate between a single major depressive episode and persistent depressive disorder?

No, I can confirm I've never had any periods of normal mood or symptom relief lasting for two weeks. While I might have a rare, single day where things feel slightly lighter, the heavy depression, foggy thinking, and guilt have been continuous and constant for over a year without any real break.
